text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page triggered -> service: infra-monitoring, incident: PD12345, urgency: high, triggered_by: alert-router, note: 'high error budget burn - redwood-runtime/us-west-2'.

pagerduty-bot: Auto-escalation configured: responders -> infra-oncall -> infra-leads -> security-team. Escalation timer: 5m.

samantha: Wait, why did this go to infra-monitoring? This alert should route to runtime-sre.

raj: I just saw two pages. I'm on vacation rotation cover, but the incident text looks like a runtime issue. @samantha are we doing a schedule override today?

angela: I pushed a temporary schedule override this morning as part of the holiday handoff for nodes maintenance — intended to send pages to runtime-sre-backup, not infra-monitoring.

mike: looks like the override target id might have been the wrong PD schedule. I see override -> schedule ID SCHED-789 (infra-monitoring).

samantha: acked. I'm taking ownership. @oncall-sre please hold paging escalation for 10m while I triage.

oncall-sre: acknowledged. Putting a temporary suppress rule for infra-monitoring alerts for 15m to avoid more noise.

raj: Paging history: PD12345 -> infra-monitoring (acked by sam) -> escalated to security-team after timer expired. That's bad, security is unrelated.

angela: omg — I must have copied the wrong schedule id from the ops runbook. I put SCHED-789 instead of SCHED-562 (runtime-sre-backup).

mike: Can we confirm customer impact? Any 5xx spikes from hosted API?

samantha: Checking dashboards now. The error spike is only on one edge cluster, ~30% increased retries, but no mass customer-facing 5xx yet. Appears degraded but not fully impacted.

raj: I see increased tail latency and a small error bump for a subset of requests to model-serving-usw2. No major traffic drop. Recommend limited mitigation and watch.

pagerduty-bot: Next escalation (security-team) still pending in 2m unless suppressed.

angela: I'm removing the override immediately and re-applying with correct schedule id. Executing: `pd schedule-override remove SCHED-789 --user angela` then `pd schedule-override add SCHED-562 --start now --end in 4h --user angela`

mike: Please paste the command output.

angela: output: "Removed override SCHED-789 (id: OV-333). Added override OV-334 -> SCHED-562."

samantha: Good. Can we also update the routing rule that caused this? There is a mapping in alert-router: `service_map['high_error_budget'] -> runtime-sre` should be verified.

raj: I opened a quick-playbook check: `/etc/alert-router/config` shows the mapping correct. The break was solely the manual override.

oncall-sre: suppress removed. No more pages expected to infra-monitoring.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD12345 marked as "acknowledged" by samantha at 1823004612.

mike: Good containment. Action: angela to run postmortem about the wrong schedule id entry and update the runbook. sam to validate if the brief misrouting caused any adhoc escalations to security that need data redaction. raj to follow up on runtime cluster error root cause separately.

angela: noted. I'll create an ops PR to add a pre-check on overrides (CLI will require a schedule-name confirmation) and update the runbook steps.

samantha: I'll contact security about the accidental page and confirm no sensitive context was shared.

raj: I'll continue to watch the metrics for 30m, and check backend logs for the error cause; will update thread if anything changes.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 -> status: acknowledged -> responder: samantha. Next steps: monitor, create follow-up ticket PD-INC-202.

mike: Temporary mitigation looks ok. No customer-major impact. Logging this as severity: S2 (partial degradation).

angela: created ticket: OPS-4021 (postmortem: wrong schedule override) and PR #657 to add CLI confirmation.

samantha: thanks everyone. Let's add a test to CI that validates schedule IDs referenced in runbooks exist and are for the intended team.

raj: 30m check-in scheduled at 1823006767.

mike: closing noise thread. If anything escalates, reopen. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed by samantha at 1823004899."
